changes.why: VAMPIRES ARE THE FUEL, NOT THE ENGINE (the pilot, 2026-11-11): blood drain, life gain, action at a distance, ferocious; pings that snowball, never a two-card infinite. Cheap answers for Oliver's turn-four table (Swords, Vanishing Verse); death and drain engines that hit each opponent or draw (Teysa, Skullclamp, Zulaport, Bastion, Elas, Falkenrath Noble, Meathook); and two loop families on Pitiless Plunderer + Ashnod's Altar — Oathsworn Vampire with Blood Artist or Zulaport, and Reassembling Skeleton (stack 013, checker-passed). Iteration 2 (2026-11-12): Utter End, Wispdrinker Vampire and Malakir Bloodwitch out for Reassembling Skeleton, Zulaport Cutthroat and Bastion of Remembrance. Forge A/B (iteration 1, 200/arm, olivers-table-nov): no resolvable difference on life removed, removal cast doubled; the AI rarely assembles the loop.

derived.name: THE OBJECTIVE
derived.what: One falsifiable threshold, written when the branch was OPENED and before anything was measured.
derived.why: Optional. When one is named it is the claim the branch made about itself, graded against its own minimum detectable difference, and it sets the rule's word. The branch is still judged on the whole profile.

derived.name: THE MANA
derived.what: Karsten's hypergeometric source targets against the pip distribution each list actually has, and the on-curve probability the base achieves.
derived.why: Deterministic, and the sampled rows cannot see it. A branch that changes its spells changes its pip distribution, so the target moves underneath the base — which is why the GAP is the figure and not the source count.

derived.name: PRIMARY AND EXPLORATORY
derived.what: The objective is the one pre-registered test. The rows are a family of looks, each with an interval on its difference, and a row's verdict is Holm-corrected across the family.
derived.why: Twelve rows at alpha 0.05 with no correction is one false 'better' in every other report. `experiment.py` pre-registers `win_rate` for the same reason. Measured over 42 tracked reports before shipping: Holm flips no verdict — the MDE rule was already near Bonferroni at the top rank — so this is what a verdict means, not which rows carry one.

derived.name: MDE
derived.what: The minimum detectable difference: the smallest gap this many games could resolve at 95% confidence.
derived.why: A row marked `noise` is NOT a row where nothing happened. It is a row where whatever happened is smaller than this run can see, which rules out a large effect and says nothing about a small one.

derived.name: THE BILL
derived.what: Every card in the branch, sorted by where it physically is: already in the deck, in a box, in another deck, or not owned.
derived.why: The only cost figure in the report. `buy` is money; `elsewhere` is a card that has to come out of a deck that is currently sleeved.

forge.answers_cast.what: removal, bounce, sweepers, edicts, fight and tax effects our seat cast or activated per game, by the card's corpus role (damage removal only on a noncreature card)
forge.answers_cast.why: whether the list answers the table, read from what the AI actually cast

forge.biggest_hit.what: the largest single-source combat damage dealt to a player, per game
forge.biggest_hit.why: one big lifelinker connecting reads differently from twelve tokens; this is the number that separates them

forge.combat_damage_dealt_to_players.what: combat damage our seat dealt to players, mean per game, with the median beside it because the sample is mostly zeros with a tail
forge.combat_damage_dealt_to_players.why: the shape of the kill on a combat deck

forge.commander_damage_max_on_one_defend.what: per game, the most combat damage one of our commanders dealt to any single opponent (21 is lethal); 0 in a game where no commander connected
forge.commander_damage_max_on_one_defend.why: the voltron clock: how close the deck gets to a commander kill, readable before the kills themselves are frequent enough to count

forge.commander_resolved_rate.what: games in which the commander resolved at least once, over games played
forge.commander_resolved_rate.why: a FLOOR on commander access under Forge's AI — the deck's plan cannot start until it does

forge.commander_uptime.what: per game: of the own turns after a commander first resolved, the share on which one was still on the battlefield (either partner), from the board series' cleanup snapshots; conditional on a commander resolving
forge.commander_uptime.why: the deck cannot start until a commander is out and cannot finish if the table keeps removing it — the recast-tax question as a figure

forge.counters_cast.what: counterspells our seat cast per game (corpus role `counterspell`)
forge.counters_cast.why: the held-up answer; the AI under-uses it, so a difference is a floor

forge.drain_dealt.what: life LOSS dealt to opponents that was not damage, per game, credited to the seat whose life-loss ability resolved last that turn; a floor
forge.drain_dealt.why: the drain engine's output, which no damage total sees

forge.eliminated_turn.what: the global turn our seat was eliminated, mean over the games it lost
forge.eliminated_turn.why: survival; conditional on losing, so a deck that wins more can read worse here for dying faster in the games it still loses

forge.empty_hand_turns.what: own turns that ended with ZERO cards in hand, per game — exact under the telemetry patch, absent on a plain record
forge.empty_hand_turns.why: the complaint itself, counted: a turn spent with nothing to rebuild with

forge.evasive_damage_share.what: share of our combat damage to players dealt by sources with flying, trample, menace or another evasion keyword, per game with any combat damage (from the deck's own keywords, so our seat only)
forge.evasive_damage_share.why: the damage that got through because it could not be blocked

forge.extra_draw_per_turn.what: cards that reached our hand from the library BEYOND the natural draw step, per own turn, per game — (library_to_hand minus one per own turn, minus nothing for the first turn on the play) over own turns; a wheel, a cantrip, a tutor and a death-trigger draw all count, a mulligan does not
forge.extra_draw_per_turn.why: the draw the DECK added, so a list that refills its hand reads apart from one that only draws for the turn; telemetry records only

forge.first_attack_turn.what: the GLOBAL turn of our seat's first declared attack, mean over the games in which it attacked at all
forge.first_attack_turn.why: how long the AI sat on the deck; conditional, so a branch that attacks in more games can read WORSE here by attacking late in games it used to skip

forge.first_wheel_turn.what: the own turn our seat's first wheel spell resolved, over games with one
forge.first_wheel_turn.why: later means a finisher rather than an opening; read beside the share above, since a deck that never wheels reads nothing here

forge.interaction_cast.what: stack objects our seat cast or activated that targeted an opponent or an opponent's permanent, once per opposing seat per object — a floor, since a permanent nobody attacked or blocked with cannot be attributed
forge.interaction_cast.why: interaction aimed at the table, of any kind; not a removal count

forge.interaction_received.what: stack objects opponents aimed at our seat or our permanents, per game, by the same rule
forge.interaction_received.why: how much of the table's interaction the list draws; lower is better

forge.kills_by_ability.what: opposing permanents that left the battlefield directly after one of our activated abilities resolved, per game, such as a -X/-X ability or an outlet's kill; a ceiling per card
forge.kills_by_ability.why: removal the deck does with its own creatures rather than with spells

forge.life_gained.what: life gained per game, all sources (the record splits it: lifelink, trigger, other)
forge.life_gained.why: the gain half of a gain/drain deck, and the input to any lifegain payoff

forge.life_removed_total.what: every point of life this seat removed from opponents in a game — combat damage plus noncombat damage plus drain, summed, with the median beside the mean because the sample has a long tail
forge.life_removed_total.why: the only axis that cannot be gamed by trading one kind of output for a smaller amount of another: a list can raise drain while losing more combat damage, and this row says so

forge.mulligans.what: mulligans our seat took per game (Forge gives the first free)
forge.mulligans.why: the kept-hand question at a table: a list the AI ships more often is one the pilot would too

forge.noncombat_damage_dealt_to_players.what: damage to players that did not come from combat, per game — an ETB pinger, a Purphoros, a direct-damage spell
forge.noncombat_damage_dealt_to_players.why: the output an ENTRY payoff produces, which needs no attack step and no blocker maths

forge.protection_cast.what: protection pieces our seat cast or activated per game (any `protection*` role)
forge.protection_cast.why: resolve: keeping the commanders and the engine on the table

forge.wheels_with_commander_share.what: of the wheel spells our seat cast, the share cast on an own turn whose cleanup board held a commander, pooled over every game (`wheel_timing`)
forge.wheels_with_commander_share.why: a wheel as a finisher dropped onto a commander, read at a table. Forge's AI fires on its own rule, so this reads whether the LIST gets a commander down before the AI's wheels fire, never the hold

forge.win_rate.what: wins over DECIDED games at the named pod (clock-outs have no winner and leave the denominator), pooled across every run of that list under one harness
forge.win_rate.why: the only figure with external validity on this bench, read against the table's null rather than a quarter

a 6+ drop out by T6.what: The share of games with a creature of mana value 6 or more on the battlefield by the end of turn 6, by any route: cast, reanimated, returned by Meren or tutored onto it.
a 6+ drop out by T6.why: The deck's payoff is its big bodies early. The pilot named it (2026-11-07): when the fatties arrive, against the turn they could be cast.

board power @T6.what: Total power on the battlefield at the end of turn 6: printed power, anthems, lords, power that reads the hand or the graveyard, and +1/+1 counters (since 2026-11-04; they had been left out). One-turn pumps and prowess have worn off.
board power @T6.why: The deck's turn-6 threat, before any of it has connected. It is what a table sees and decides to answer, and it moves earlier than damage does.

damage @T10.scale: one turn's damage, so 40.0 would be lethal in a single swing from an opponent at full life — not a total across the game
damage @T10.what: Damage dealt to the single goldfish opponent ON turn 10, averaged over every game — the clock at its tenth turn, not a running total. THE SWING AND WHAT FIRES AROUND IT: combat damage, attack triggers, arrival and burn. IT EXCLUDES the payoffs on a discard or a draw and the drain; `output.total_damage_by_turn` in the diagnostic is the figure with them (not a row: it tracks this one game for game, one measurement twice). The cumulative series does not exist for this pillar; `mean_cumulative_event_damage_by_turn` is the only running total the model keeps, and it covers event damage alone.
damage @T10.why: The headline output figure and the one a doubler moves. It has no ceiling, so unlike the kill rate it keeps separating two lists after both of them already win.

dead wheels in hand @T5.scale: against the cards in hand at the end of turn 5
dead wheels in hand @T5.what: Wheel cards held at the end of turn 5 while no discard or draw payoff is on the battlefield, averaged over every game; zero whenever a payoff is out.
dead wheels in hand @T5.why: The clog: a hand of wheels with little else to play, as a number. It rises with the wheel count and with a hold policy, which is the point — a branch that cuts wheels is graded here, and a branch that cannot land a commander shows up here before it shows up in damage.

experience @T7.scale: against the mana values she returns: a 6-drop needs six
experience @T7.what: Meren of Clan Nel Toth's experience counters at the end of turn 7, averaged over every game: one for every other creature of ours that died while she was out.
experience @T7.why: Her end step returns the biggest creature card in the graveyard to the BATTLEFIELD only if its mana value is within her experience, otherwise to hand. This is the clock on the free returns.

extra cards by T8.scale: against the 8 cards every deck draws for free by then
extra cards by T8.what: Cards drawn BEYOND the one-a-turn draw step, cumulative to the end of turn 8, averaged over every game. Counts only draw the model can price — a card's own ETB draw, an instant or sorcery that draws, an upkeep trigger, a trigger that draws when other creatures or tokens enter, and (since 2026-10-19) a trigger that draws when a creature dies, on the deaths the sacrifice and death channels produce and no others, activated draws at the end of the main phase while spare mana pays and X-cost draw spells with what is left (2026-11-04: this said those were not counted, and they have been). A draw whose cost has no reader ('you may pay 2 life. If you do') is NOT counted, and the card is named in the goldfish artifact.
extra cards by T8.why: A board with nothing in hand has no way to rebuild, and until 2026-08-28 the model could not see it: it drew one card a turn whatever the list said. Read it against the count of draw cards, not alone — a deck listing twelve draw sources whose modelled figure is one has almost no UNCONDITIONAL card advantage, and that is a fact about the deck rather than a limit of the parser.

finisher wheel by T8.scale: against the games themselves — one finisher per game counts, however many wheels followed it
finisher wheel by T8.what: The share of games in which, by the end of turn 8, a wheel resolved with a COMMANDER on the battlefield. (Until 2026-11-04 it also needed four nonlands left in hand, which the model's deploy-first turn now spends before it wheels.) Spell wheels and activated wheels both count; the discard wheels the model cannot parse are named in the goldfish declaration and are in no figure here.
finisher wheel by T8.why: A wheel played as a finisher dropped onto a commander rather than as early tempo. Under a hold policy every wheel waits for a commander, so this row is when the first one LANDS, and a list that cannot get a commander down with a wheel in hand by turn 8 reads low here before it reads low anywhere else.

hand can act by T3.scale: against the keep rate itself — this is a property of the seven cards kept, assuming no draws
hand can act by T3.what: The share of kept opening hands containing a nonland card the hand's own lands can pay for by turn three, counting at most three land drops and no draws.
hand can act by T3.why: A stricter threshold than the 2-5 lands rule the model actually mulligans by, and it is REPORTED rather than enforced, so it cannot restate a figure on any deck. It separates "this hand had lands" from "this hand could do something" — the distinction behind a two-land keep that never got going.

hoard @T10.what: Treasures still standing at the END of turn 10, after the turn has spent what it spent, averaged over every game. (Until 2026-11-04 the number was read before the turn's spending, under this same label.)
hoard @T10.why: The second axis, and the only one that is not combat. It is near-uncorrelated with damage, power and kill (r = 0.08-0.25 across the fleet), so it can fall while they rise and mean it.

hoard @T6.what: The same count at the end of turn 6 — the hoard you actually have when the deck wants to deploy, rather than the one you end up with.
hoard @T6.why: A big turn-10 hoard that was not there on turn 6 arrived too late to cast anything that mattered.

interaction affordable @T6.scale: conditional on holding one — the denominator is games where an answer was in hand, not all games
interaction affordable @T6.what: Of the games where an answer was in hand on turn 6, the share where the turn also ended with enough unspent mana to cast it, or where it is free for controlling a commander and one is out. The suite is removal + sweepers + protection, the same set `deck-audit` counts.
interaction affordable @T6.why: Whether the deck can spend its mana developing and still hold up the answer in its hand. It is CONDITIONAL on purpose: the raw castable rate falls when you simply cut interaction, which answers a different question. Measured at the END OF THE MAIN PHASE, before combat is paid for. And it is a FLOOR — the model casts everything it can afford every turn, so a pilot choosing to hold up scores higher.

kept hand passes the pilot's keep rule.scale: against the keep rate itself — a property of the seven cards kept, assuming no draws
kept hand passes the pilot's keep rule.what: The share of kept opening hands that the pilot's own keep rule (`pilot_policy.json`, verb `keep`: a cap per class, one card of a needed class) would also have kept.
kept hand passes the pilot's keep rule.why: REPORTED and never enforced, so it cannot restate a figure on any deck, and absent on a deck that has written no rule. It prices how often the list deals a seven the pilot would ship.

killed by T10.scale: a CLOCK against one unblocking opponent, never a win rate
killed by T10.what: The same, by the end of turn 10 — the harness's last turn.
killed by T10.why: Whether the deck closes at all. It saturates near 1.0, so on a list that already wins it stops discriminating and damage @T10 is the honest axis instead.

killed by T6.scale: a CLOCK against one unblocking opponent, never a win rate
killed by T6.what: The share of games in which cumulative damage reaches 40 by the end of turn 6.
killed by T6.why: THE CLOCK, at the turn a real pod is still setting up. This is the figure a faster list is bought for.

missed drop by T5.what: The share of games that miss at least one land drop across turns 1 to 5.
missed drop by T5.why: The single best predictor of a slow start, and the row most sensitive to a land count change.

mulliganed.what: The share of games that took at least one mulligan under the harness rule: keep a 7 with 2-5 lands, up to two redraws.
mulliganed.why: A proxy for whether the land count fits the curve. It should barely move unless the land count did.

stall, 2 in a row.what: The share of games with two consecutive turns, from turn 2 on, where nothing in hand could be cast with the mana available.
stall, 2 in a row.why: Two dead turns in a row is how a deck loses without ever being interacted with. Curve and colour problems both surface here.

turns saved on big bodies.scale: turns, summed over the 5+ drops that entered in a game
turns saved on big bodies.what: For every creature of mana value 5+ that entered by turn 10, the turns between its arrival and the first turn that game's own mana could have cast it (11 if it never could), floored at zero; summed per game, averaged.
turns saved on big bodies.why: The cheat dividend: what the graveyard engine buys over hard-casting. A hard-cast body saves nothing; a turn-3 Animate Dead on a turn-8 Archon saves five.

wheels cast by T10.scale: against the wheel-shaped cards the declaration names
wheels cast by T10.what: Wheels resolved — spell or activated — cumulative to the end of turn 10, averaged over every game.
wheels cast by T10.why: A wheel engine's trigger count: a discard or draw payoff has nothing to do until a hand empties. Reported with a direction for the report's sake, but the table's dislike of a wheel is in no figure here — this counts what the model fired, not what a pod forgave — so read it beside the finisher row, never alone.

design.correction: Holm step-down over the exploratory rows
design.rule: a row is better/worse only if its delta clears the MDE AND its |z| survives Holm across the family; the objective is graded on its own, uncorrected, because it was declared before the measurement

branch.reads_as: every Forge run on the branch was made with a different list, so this rate describes that list. A card swap and a cosmetic edit to decklist.txt both land here. Re-run: `manamap pilot simulate edgar-vampires@threat-v1 --pod <name> --games N`

limits: The goldfish has no opponents and nothing blocks: its kill turn is a CLOCK, not a win rate, and it cannot see interaction, removal or any alternate win.
Nothing here reads `goldfish_targets.json`'s `required` flags. The engine lift did, and was deleted for it: the declaration is authored, so the same hand set the target and read the verdict.

Card advantage is measured only where the model can price it. Activated, X-based, sacrifice-gated and death-triggered draw are unmodelled and named per deck in `goldfish_metrics.json`; on a sacrifice-based list that is most of it.

Deaths ARE modelled here, at a MEASURED rate: 0.858 of our creatures and 1.3118 of theirs per own turn, read off forge run sythis-enchantress-vs-jarad-graveyard-vs-abaddon-n200-da677689-s20261001-memm-edgar-vampires-podExperimental-c600-ov8c347642-aif7c3b6a8-tl9473cf35 (standard-v3, 2026-10-01, list 7be137d0 = V3): 200 games, 1728 own creature deaths (1016 of them tokens) and 2642 opponent creature deaths over 2014 own turns, counted from every `Zone Change: … was put into Graveyard from Battlefield` line whose card is a creature or a creature token, seats matched by label suffix across the rotating jobs. Both the life-loss idiom (`death_drain`) and the damage idiom (`death_damage`) are counted. The rate is an AVERAGE, so it cannot represent a turn where eight bodies die at once — a sacrifice burst is still understated.

mana.note: Deterministic, not sampled — Karsten's tables against the pip distribution each list actually has. No interval, because there is no sampling error to carry.

recommendation.because: No guard was named, so nothing here grades the branch — only what changed: read the rows as a whole profile.

cost.reads_as: 5 to buy; 3 to pull out of a deck that is still together; 92 of 97 already owned

notes: Forge, against a real pod: +0.020 win rate, CI [-0.051, +0.092] — this run cannot separate the two lists.

reward.why_we_care: The second axis, and the only one that is not combat. It is near-uncorrelated with damage, power and kill (r = 0.08-0.25 across the fleet), so it can fall while they rise and mean it.
A big turn-10 hoard that was not there on turn 6 arrived too late to cast anything that mattered.

table.method: paired t interval on 10,000 game-by-game differences (same seed per game)
table.what: Treasures still standing at the END of turn 10, after the turn has spent what it spent, averaged over every game. (Until 2026-11-04 the number was read before the turn's spending, under this same label.)
table.why_we_care: The second axis, and the only one that is not combat. It is near-uncorrelated with damage, power and kill (r = 0.08-0.25 across the fleet), so it can fall while they rise and mean it.

table.method: paired t interval on 10,000 game-by-game differences (same seed per game)
table.what: The same count at the end of turn 6 — the hoard you actually have when the deck wants to deploy, rather than the one you end up with.
table.why_we_care: A big turn-10 hoard that was not there on turn 6 arrived too late to cast anything that mattered.

table.method: paired t interval on 10,000 game-by-game differences (same seed per game)
table.scale: one turn's damage, so 40.0 would be lethal in a single swing from an opponent at full life — not a total across the game
table.what: Damage dealt to the single goldfish opponent ON turn 10, averaged over every game — the clock at its tenth turn, not a running total. THE SWING AND WHAT FIRES AROUND IT: combat damage, attack triggers, arrival and burn. IT EXCLUDES the payoffs on a discard or a draw and the drain; `output.total_damage_by_turn` in the diagnostic is the figure with them (not a row: it tracks this one game for game, one measurement twice). The cumulative series does not exist for this pillar; `mean_cumulative_event_damage_by_turn` is the only running total the model keeps, and it covers event damage alone.
table.why_we_care: The headline output figure and the one a doubler moves. It has no ceiling, so unlike the kill rate it keeps separating two lists after both of them already win.

table.method: paired t interval on 10,000 game-by-game differences (same seed per game)
table.scale: against the 8 cards every deck draws for free by then
table.what: Cards drawn BEYOND the one-a-turn draw step, cumulative to the end of turn 8, averaged over every game. Counts only draw the model can price — a card's own ETB draw, an instant or sorcery that draws, an upkeep trigger, a trigger that draws when other creatures or tokens enter, and (since 2026-10-19) a trigger that draws when a creature dies, on the deaths the sacrifice and death channels produce and no others, activated draws at the end of the main phase while spare mana pays and X-cost draw spells with what is left (2026-11-04: this said those were not counted, and they have been). A draw whose cost has no reader ('you may pay 2 life. If you do') is NOT counted, and the card is named in the goldfish artifact.
table.why_we_care: A board with nothing in hand has no way to rebuild, and until 2026-08-28 the model could not see it: it drew one card a turn whatever the list said. Read it against the count of draw cards, not alone — a deck listing twelve draw sources whose modelled figure is one has almost no UNCONDITIONAL card advantage, and that is a fact about the deck rather than a limit of the parser.
